_note: PLACEHOLDER DIALOGUE. Please have local Elders and community (e.g. the Metropolitan Local Aboriginal Land Council) review, rewrite and own these words before release. Characters are fictional.

intro.text: Welcome, bub. Come sit by the fire. Before you do anything in this city, know where you're standing.
This is Gadigal land, of the Eora Nation. Always was, always will be. Say it with your chest.
Culture isn't something locked in a museum. It's how we know who we are — our families, our languages, our stories, and our responsibilities to Country and to each other.
Our people have cared for this Country for more than sixty thousand years. Every generation carries it forward. Now it's your turn to carry it.
This place — The Block — has been a heart for our mob in the city for a long time. People came here to find family, to organise, to look after one another.
In 1938, just up the road at Australian Hall on Elizabeth Street, our people held the Day of Mourning. They stood up when it was hard. You're part of that line.
Now listen close. A movement is only as strong as its trust. Some will wear blue and smile at you — but they're Reds, spies for the Crown.
They'll spread rumours and break up your rallies. Watch each other. Yarn it out in the Yarning Circle — press V — and vote them out of the City.
Lobby with real voices. Get real people to sign the petition — every ten names turns a politician from red to blue. A hundred opens the next part of the city.
And walk together. A thousand of you and City Council has to listen. Ten thousand, and Macquarie Street belongs to the people.
When the crowd reaches Town Hall, get up on that stage. Speak, read your poem, play your music. Let them hear your heart.
Before you go — let's see what you've learnt.

quiz.q: Whose land is the Sydney CBD on?
options: The Gadigal people of the Eora Nation
quiz.right: That's right. Gadigal land. Always was, always will be.
quiz.wrong: Not quite, bub. It's Gadigal land, of the Eora Nation.

quiz.q: What do the colours of the Aboriginal flag stand for?
options: Black for the people, red for the earth and our spiritual connection to it, yellow for the sun
quiz.right: Deadly. Harold Thomas designed it, and it first flew in 1971.
quiz.wrong: Black is the people, red is the earth and our spiritual relationship to it, and yellow is the sun — the giver of life.

quiz.q: Where was the 1938 Day of Mourning held?
quiz.right: Yes. Go visit it — it's marked on your map.
quiz.wrong: It was at Australian Hall on Elizabeth Street, right here in Sydney. Go and see it.

farewell.text: Go peacefully. Go strong. Look after each other.
And come back and tell us what you've learnt. We'll be right here by the fire.

again.text: Good to see you again. How's the movement going? Remember — trust is everything.
Keep getting those signatures. Real voices change minds.
